title: Qualitative Codebook, Case Audit, and Integration Record
paragraphs: Appendix F Qualitative Codebook, Case Audit, and Integration Record The coding unit is one supplied researcher-recorded encounter. Codes can cooccur. Observations and recorded remarks supply evidence; researcher reections supply contextual interpretation only. The full machine-readable codebook, case memos, source hashes, and joined audit are preserved in the thematic codebook, the case-level coding record, the coding-provenance record, and the mixed-methods verication record. T1: Grounds for credibility Include source use, correction, neutrality, explanation, viewpoint diversity, peer review, or ratings as explicit judgment cues. Exclude generic praise and unqualied technical clarity. T2: Peer connection Include natural student speech, familiarity, friendship, authenticity, or solidarity. Exclude an interface preference without a peer connection. T3: Situated listening value Include calm, fatigue, quiet appreciation, limited time, concision, structure, or 264

APPENDIX F. QUALITATIVE CODEBOOK, CASE AUDIT, AND INTEGRATION RECORD 265 immersion. A recorded duration alone is insucient. T4: Participatory agency Include voting, topic control, creator aspirations, co-creation, privacy conditions, or contribution to platform improvement. Distinguish recorded actions from future intentions. T5: Student-lived relevance Include explicit campus, work, study, career, local-mobility, or civic interests. Do not infer preferences from faculty membership alone. T6: Enabling delivery and interface Include experienced continuity, audio clarity, latency, visual integration, controls, or usability. Do not code such praise as independently measured accuracy or engineering quality. The additional qualitative records are SR0029, SR0043, SR0044, SR0046, SR0051, SR0054, SR0057, and SR0058. No in the following table means not in the historical quantitative subset, not invalid qualitative evidence. CSV identiers are reproduced exactly. The prole document's shorter zero-padding must not be silently substituted during joins.

APPENDIX F. QUALITATIVE CODEBOOK, CASE AUDIT, AND INTEGRATION RECORD 267 F.1 Audit and Interpretive Scope The coding was performed by the researcher and reviewed during thesis revision. No independent-coder statistics, member checking, or saturation assessment were performed for these 60 rider records. A separate 193-segment FGD/self-report codebook validation is reported in Section 6.12.15. The coding matrix, source excerpts, and case memos preserve the basis for examining alternative readings. The record does not establish that every recorded remark is a verbatim transcript. Interpretive disagreement is distinct from an error in recounting code frequencies. A numerical recount can reproduce the coding matrix; it cannot independently validate the interpretive choices.
